images.caption:
A photo of an electric bug zapper which appears to be of a very old design. The photo was taken during a visit to the Museum of American Heritage where the zapper was on display. This zapper appears to consist of an assembly incorporating a light bulb surrounded by windings of fine wire with a second, much smaller light bulb near to the larger bulb. The zapper assembly has an Edison screw base extending from one end so that the assembly can draw power from an existing light bulb socket.


This Collectors Weekly page shows a zapper that is similar (possibly the same model) and which has a paper cylinder fitted between the bulbs and the wire windings. In addition, the WorthPoint site has an entry for a "DEATH RAY LANTERN" bug zapper (with a model number of 1938) that is similar to (or perhaps the same model as) the zapper that is shown on this page.

images.caption: A photo of an old electric Ziff-O-Lec immersion heater. The photo was taken during a visit to the Museum of American Heritage where the heater was on display. From what one understands, this device has an enameled outside and would be immersed in a container of water to heat it. The heater has a twisted-wire power cord with cloth covered wires and the plug is fitted with an Edison screw base adapter so that the heater can easily be powered from a light bulb socket. According to this Ebay sale page, a version of the Ziff-O-Lec heater was patented in 1921 and produced by the Ziff Electric company of Los Angeles, California.
